spans.text: Tokarev's visual module slowly reboots, the scattered blur of lights gathering bit by bit into a clear image.

She finds herself lying in the corner of the Elmo's ops room, a slightly worn blanket draped over her. Only the emergency lights are on inside the cabin, their dim amber glow making the whole space feel unusually quiet.
Not far away, Kalina's silhouette sits before the main console. The monitors cast a ghostly blue light across her tired but focused face.
Her fingers dance rapidly across the keyboard. She seems completely absorbed in whatever she's looking through.
Tokarev tries to sit up. A faint mechanical scrape comes from her joints. Kalina instantly turns her head and, seeing Tokarev awake, drops everything she's doing and hurries over.
You're awake! How do you feel? Is your system running normally?
System is functioning normally...
Just still a little... sluggish.
Tokarev straightens herself. Her finger joints click softly as she flexes her arms, confirming all functions have returned.
Kalina crouches beside her, worry and guilt written all over her face.
Tokarev, I'm really, really sorry.
I shouldn't have reactivated you so recklessly...
The neural cloud malfunction struck again, didn't it? This is all my fault.
Tokarev studies Kalina's exhausted expression and gently shakes her head.
No, Miss Kalina, this isn't because of anything you did.
A similar issue already occurred even before the Commander's operation.
Please don't blame yourself.
I... am fine.
Kalina exhales in relief, though the worry in her eyes doesn't fully fade.
She reaches out and brushes aside a few loose strands of hair from Tokarev's forehead, like tending to a sick child.
If anything feels off again, you must tell me.
We can go back to the city and have a professional technician look at you.

Tokarev glances around the ops room, taking in the blinking indicators across the control panels and the active screens. This is a completely different sight from the Elmo's powered-down state when they left it.
I remember... they cut the power to the Elmo.
How did you restart the system?
A hint of smug pride lifts Kalina's expression. She seems to forget her fatigue for a moment.
Ah, well.
Even though the main power was cut remotely, I checked the main control system and found that the Elmo has an independent emergency backup.
As long as you bypass the remote lockouts, you can bring the basic systems online again.
She tilts her chin up proudly, eyes sparkling with mischief.
Don't forget, I'm Griffin's Logistics Officer.
I know these systems better than anyone!
Tokarev nods, genuinely impressed. Even in a situation like this, Kalina never fails to demonstrate an astounding level of professional competence.
You really do live up to your reputation, Miss Kalina...
By the way, how long was I out?
Kalina checks her watch.
About four hours.
When you suddenly collapsed, I was terrified...
Luckily the Elmo has simple Doll diagnostic tools. Once I confirmed it was just temporary neural cloud overload, I let you sleep it off.
...Four hours.
Then time is running short. We need to—
Before she can finish, Kalina grabs Tokarev's hand with sudden excitement, cutting her off.
Tokarev! I'm onto something!
While you were resting, I reviewed the Elmo's internal system logs!
She pulls Tokarev toward the main console, pointing at the stream of data flickering past the screens.
Look—according to the logs, the Elmo's system was activated before we arrived!
And not just once!
When?
Kalina taps the keyboard, bringing up a more detailed report.
The most recent activation was early yesterday morning, just a few hours after the explosion.
Someone bypassed the main power cutoff, activated the backup system, and accessed the Elmo's main database.
Can you determine who it was?
Kalina shakes her head with a frown.
The access logs were wiped—almost nothing remains.
Whoever did it knows the Elmo's architecture extremely well.
She opens another window showing a list of directories that were accessed.
They didn't delete or modify anything. They seemed to be... searching for something.
...Do you think this could be related to the Commander's "death"?
Kalina bites her lip while she mulls this over.
I bet it is.
This person was probably looking for the Commander—or...
Checking to see whether the Commander had left anything behind.
But I can't determine who they are or what their intentions were.
All I know is they understand both the Elmo and the Commander very well.
They could be from the Military... or someone inside IOP?
Could even be someone from Griffin... or—
She pauses abruptly, eyes widening.
Or it could be the Commander themself!
If the Commander didn't actually die, but managed to escape after the explosion and didn't want to be found...
The first thing they'd do is destroy or secure anything that could reveal their location!
But if that's the case, why only erase the access logs?
Why not delete the data? That wouldn't hide their trail at all...
It would only expose the fact that the Commander came back here.
Kalina's excitement dims a little.
...You're right. I'm getting ahead of myself.
They fall into a brief silence.
Kalina is the first to break it.
...Regardless, we need to keep investigating.
We're heading to the White Zone to examine the blast site. That's the real key to finding the Commander.
...Yes.
But the White Zone's security checks will be a problem.
Then we'll just have to deal with it.
Prep your weapon and ammunition. We're moving out.
